topic: Intake Breathing Gets $62M for Magnetic Nasal Strips

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Intake Breathing Gets $62M for Magnetic Nasal Strips

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Camino Partners, the investment firm founded by Kind Snacks creator Daniel Lubetzky, is backing the nasal breathing brand as it looks to expand into mainstream retail Intake Breathing has received a $62 million investment from Camino Partners, the investment firm founded by Kind Snacks creator Daniel Lubetzky, as the nasal breathing brand looks to capitalize on growing consumer interest in sleep, recovery and performance optimization. The investment marks Intake’s first significant outside capital infusion, taking the family-run business into its next phase of growth with a partner experienced in building consumer brands. Founded by inventor and medical device engineer Jim Castillo and led by his son-in-law, co-founder and CEO Alex Hauck, Intake makes a magnetic nasal dilator designed to open the nasal passages and improve airflow. Unlike traditional adhesive nasal strips, Intake’s system uses a reusable magnetic band and adhesive tabs to mechanically open the nasal valve, the narrowest part of the nasal airway. “Intake started as a solution to a problem in my father-in-law’s own garage, and it’s become something bigger than we ever imagined,” Hauck said.

en.headline: Intake Breathing Gets $62M for Magnetic Nasal Strips

topic: Garmin Fitness Revenue Climbs 16% After Screenless Wearable Launch

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Garmin Fitness Revenue Climbs 16% After Screenless Wearable Launch

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Garmin posted another strong quarter for its fitness business, with its new screenless smart band positioning it to compete more directly with Whoop. The wearable technology giant posted another strong quarter for its fitness business, with its new screenless smart band positioning it to compete more directly with Whoop Garmin’s fitness business continues to grow, with third-quarter revenue climbing 16% year over year to $694 million as the company expands its presence in the competitive wearable technology market. The growth was driven by strong demand for wearables, according to Garmin, which reported record companywide revenue and operating income for the quarter ended Sept. 26. Fitness remained Garmin’s largest business segment by revenue, generating $231 million in operating income with an operating margin of 33%. The results come as Garmin makes a bigger push into everyday health and wellness tracking, highlighted by the July launch of its $199.99 Cirqa Smart Band, a screenless wearable designed to compete with Whoop and other fitness trackers. Unlike Whoop, which requires a paid membership, Cirqa offers health and fitness tracking without a subscription. Garmin CEO Cliff Pemble has previously pointed to the company’s extensive features and subscription-free model as competitive advantages in the increasingly crowded wearables market.

en.headline: Garmin Fitness Revenue Climbs 16% After Screenless Wearable Launch

topic: How One Fitness Operator Tripled Recovery Engagement Metrics

facts.label: Story
facts.value: How One Fitness Operator Tripled Recovery Engagement Metrics

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Ozwell Fitness turned recovery into a habit with Neo Science's wellness tech, driving thousands of sessions and stronger member engagement One Indiana health club has turned recovery into a habit with Neo Science’s premium wellness technology, driving thousands of sessions and stronger member engagement Gemi Ozdemir had grown tired of running around town to get his wellness fix. For red light therapy, he had to go to one venue. To see his personal trainer, he’d have to go to another. Then, to get a sweat in at the sauna, he’d have to go to a third place. “It was fragmented,” Ozdemir said. “It was hard to keep up with.” Determined to create the convenience he couldn’t find elsewhere, Ozdemir eventually launched Ozwell Fitness, a premier health club in Carmel, Indiana. There, he did everything he could to bring all those services under one roof. “The whole idea was a more efficient wellness routine: work out and recover in one place,” he explained. Soon, Ozdemir realized he wasn’t the only one frustrated with a lack of consolidated wellness offerings. After assembling his own with Ozwell, he attracted thousands of new customers and even tripled usage rates for some services. “Our retention is strong,” he said.

facts.value: It’s with deep sorrow that we join the Cooper Aerobics community — and the wider health and fitness industry — in mourning the passing of Dr. Tyler Cooper. He died October 21 after a nine-month battle with acute myeloid leukemia. “We are heartbroken to share the passing of Dr. Tyler C. Cooper — a devoted leader, proud father and passionate adventurer,” said Cooper Aerobics in a social media post. “From climbing mountains on all seven continents to summiting all 74 14,000‑ft. peaks in the contiguous U.S., he lived life with extraordinary energy and purpose. As president and CEO, he championed the Cooper mission worldwide, leading major renovations, expanding international partnerships and advancing innovations like the CooperFit cardiovascular test. His impact on health, wellness and preventive medicine will be felt for generations. The entire Cooper Aerobics family mourns this tremendous loss. Prayers are with his entire family, including his wife, Angie, and their three children, Dr. & Mrs. Kenneth Cooper and his sister Berkley and her family.” Tyler grew up at the renowned Cooper Aerobics Center in Dallas, which was founded by his father, Kenneth H. Cooper, MD, MPH, just eight days before Tyler was born. Since childhood, engaging in health and wellness activities was always apart of his life.

topic: [Garmin Q3 2026 Earnings Call] Garmin Raises Full-Year Outlook as Q3 Revenue Tops $1.98B and EPS Jumps 39% to $2.76

facts.label: Story
facts.value: [Garmin Q3 2026 Earnings Call] Garmin Raises Full-Year Outlook as Q3 Revenue Tops $1.98B and EPS Jumps 39% to $2.76

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Add preferred source Garmin delivered a record-breaking third quarter of 2026, with revenue climbing 12% year-over-year to $1.986 billion and pro forma earnings per share surging 39% to $2.76, far ahead of consensus. Gross margin expanded 420 basis points to 63.3%, fueled by favorable segment mix, a weaker Taiwan dollar, and $33 million in tariff refunds. Operating income jumped 34% to $612 million, lifting operating margin to 30.8%. The fitness segment led with 16% growth to $694 million, while outdoor revenue rose 20% to $597 million on strong demand for the new fēnix 9 series. Marine grew 16% to $310 million, aviation added 5% to $253 million, and auto OEM fell 20% as expected. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, now projecting revenue of approximately $8.15 billion, a 61% gross margin, a 29% operating margin, and pro forma EPS of $10.80. However, executives cautioned that 2027 gross margins will likely revert to the historical 58-59% range due to rising memory costs and an unfavorable mix shift from the Mercedes-Benz domain controller ramp, pledging to offset pressures through vertical integration, scale, and selective pricing. Key Elements Garmin Ltd.
